question.text: For a given chemical reaction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>300</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math> the free energy change is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>49</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and the enthalpy of reaction is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>51</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kJ</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> The entropy change of the reaction is _________<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>JK</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math>

solution.text:
Given chemical reaction:

A⟶T=300 KB[ΔG]P,T=-49.4 kJ/mol

ΔHrxn=51.4 kJ/mol

ΔSrxn=?

⇒From the relation [ΔG]P,T=ΔH-TΔS

⇒ΔSrxn=ΔHrxn-[ΔG]P,TT

=[51.4-(-49.4)]×1000300JmolK

⇒ΔSrxn=336JmolK
